history.summary: IDENTITY UNCONFIRMED - PROVISIONAL ENTRY: No web source documents a specific temple called 'Dhobi Bazaar Mandir' in Bathinda. Dhobi Bazaar is Bathinda's historic main shopping market, not a temple locality: per the Bathinda Development Authority master-plan report, the first planned development on Bathinda's city map was Rajinder Ganj Mandi (established 1885 by the then ruler of Patiala state), and this old mandi area is the present-day commercial core known as Dhobi Bazaar, Bank Bazaar, Post Office Bazaar, Hospital Bazaar and Sadar Bazaar, near Mall Road. The bazaar is well documented as a shopping destination (Tripadvisor, travelsetu) but no mandir under this exact name has any listing, review, article or map entry. Possibilities: (a) a small local shrine inside the market with no web footprint; (b) a CSV naming artifact for some other Bathinda temple (e.g. the Maiser Khana temple ~29 km from Bathinda dedicated to Jawala Ji, whose origin tale of a pilgrim named Kamal appears in a Bathinda travel piece - but that is a different, well-documented temple, not this row); (c) a non-temple record. Deities, antiquity, festivals and timings are therefore left blank rather than invented. RECOMMENDATION: field verification by the dataset owner - confirm whether a shrine of this name exists in Dhobi Bazaar; merge with an existing entry or drop if it is a market-area label.

name: Dhobi Bazaar Mandir
town: Bathinda (CSV town correct - Dhobi Bazaar is a market locality in Bathinda city; the temple identity itself is unverified)
town_description: Dhobi Bazaar is the old commercial heart of Bathinda city (the 1885 Rajinder Ganj Mandi planned by the Patiala ruler), a dense network of shops near Mall Road selling clothes, footwear, jewellery and household goods, known for bargaining and street food. Bathinda itself is a historic Malwa-region city of Punjab (~2.85 lakh population, 2011), famous for the ancient Qila Mubarak fort, the Haji Rattan dargah complex, and its thermal-power and rail-junction heritage.
tradition: Hindu (assumed from the CSV name - UNVERIFIED)

travel.airport: Bathinda Airport (BUP) has limited commercial service; Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (~190 km) is the nearest major airport.
travel.railway: Bathinda Junction, one of the largest rail junctions of North India (connected to Hisar, Ambala, Delhi, Bikaner, Ferozepur, Fazilka since 1890), then local transport to Dhobi Bazaar near Mall Road.
travel.road: Dhobi Bazaar is in Bathinda's old city, off Mall Road; reachable by auto-rickshaw or e-rickshaw from Bathinda Junction (~3 km).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (Punjab plains are extremely hot April-June).
